speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long the nosebleeds and skin spots have been happening, and have you noticed any bleeding from the gums or heavy bruising?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any fever, bone pain, or swollen lymph nodes in the child? Also, has he had any recent viral infections or been exposed to new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall any recent viral illness, and has the child experienced any fever, bone pain, or noticeable swelling of the lymph nodes? I would also like to know if there is any history of excessive bleeding after minor injuries or surgeries in the family.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if the child has had any recent viral illness, fever, or bone pain, and is there a family history of bleeding disorders? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_and_Peripheral_Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Note: Additional coagulation studies (PT 12s, aPTT 30s) were normal, but Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay) revealed platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors, consistent with Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The special test results confirming a deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors explain the bleeding despite normal platelet counts. This pattern is diagnostic for a specific inherited platelet function disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia
